newsitem.title: IRAN: Wealthy Iranians can use American toothpaste.
newsitem.headline: Wealthy Iranians can use American toothpaste.

text.p: Wealthy Iranians can still, at a price, buy at least one American luxury in the shops of downtown Tehran -- toothpaste all the way from Cincinnati.
American goods are still on offer in Tehran shops despite a clampdown by Iranian authorities on goods imported from the U.S. and Washington's trade sanctions against Tehran.
A tube of Procter and Gamble's Crest-brand toothpaste is sold at 15,000 rials ($5 at the official exchange rate) compared to Iran's home-made Darougar brand which retails at just 220 rials.

The price of the U.S. tube becomes even more startling when it becomes clear that the same 15,000 rials can get you 90 litres of unleaded Iranian petrol, or a satisfying meal for two or even a mongrel puppy dog from a street-trader.
Even a packet of 20 Mild Seven cigarettes officially imported from Japan under licence costs just 3,500 rials.
"It comes from Dubai...It's very good," said one shopowner offering a range of Western-made toiletries in an office district of central Tehran.
Dubai, a small trading emirate in the United Arab Emirates which is Iran's Arab neighbour across the Gulf, is a main re-export centre for a range of Western consumer goods to Iran.

The ships travelling from Dubai to Iranian ports, together with imports and smuggling from Turkey and the former republics of the Soviet Union bring a host of goods into Iran which are officially outlawed but tolerated.

Tehran's cleric-led government, ever sensitive to what it calls Western "cultural invasion", has made widespread efforts with limited success to stop the smuggling of U.S. music videos and film cassettes into the country.

Similarly Washington has sought to stop the export of U.S. goods, particularly electronics, to the Islamic republic which it accuses of being the world's biggest sponsor of international terrorism. Tehran denies the charges.
On the evidence of kiosks across Tehran, selling Philip Morris Marlboro cigarettes for 5,000 rials a pack, the crackdown by both sides is not completely watertight.
